transcript:
Meeting header: 
Date: 2026-03-04 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Priya Kaur (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Auriga Head Eng), Jared Kim (Auriga ML Eng), Priyanka Rao (Auriga CTO)

Summary (auto): quick Hosted API walkthrough — streaming, params, retries; customer constraints: 99th % latency, cost per 1M tokens, data retention / compliance.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I'm Samir from Redwood, with Priya our SE. How are you all doing?
[00:06] Marta: Good, thanks. Excited to see the hosted demo. We had a look at the deck you sent.
[00:10] Priya: Great. Quick agenda — we’ll run through the Hosted API for chat/text generation, show streaming, parameters tuning, and how retries/workflows look, then leave time for Q&A.
[00:20] Jared: Sounds good, main things for us are latency at peak, cost, and how streaming would work in our web chat.
[00:25] Priya: Totally. For context, can you remind us of your targets? Marta?
[00:29] Marta: Sure — user-facing chat, target p95 < 500ms, p99 ideally < 900ms. Typical message length is 50-120 tokens but sometimes we have longer context ~600 tokens. Throughput averages 1k messages/day with spikes to 2k-3k per hour during promos.
[00:45] Priya: Good to know. Hosted API has streaming and non-streaming paths; streaming helps perceived latency for users since partial tokens can be flushed as they're generated. We'll demo that.
[00:55] Priya: (shares screen) Here's the quick example using our Node SDK — you can create a chat completion call and set stream: true. We pipe the events back to the frontend, so the UI shows tokens in real time.
[01:15] Samir: One note — streaming is supported over HTTP2 and websocket; SDK handles the event parsing so you don't need to manage chunk boundaries.
[01:25] Priya: Example snippet: client.chat.completions.create({ model: 'redwood-chat-medium', messages: [...], stream: true, temperature: 0.2, max_tokens: 150 }) — stream events are incremental text delta and final event with usage.
[01:43] Jared: When streaming, how does billing work? Are we billed per token as final output or per streamed chunk?
[01:49] Priya: Billed per token generated and input tokens. Streaming doesn't change billing; it's just a transport optimization. If you stop early you’re billed for what was generated up to that point.
[02:02] Priyanka: And what about retries — e.g., network hiccup mid-stream?
[02:07] Priya: Good question. For streaming, we recommend a short idempotency key and checkpointing on your client. If the stream dies, client retries with same idempotency key so server can return a final cached result or resume where feasible. For short simple calls we often just retry non-streaming to get a clean response.
[02:28] Samir: We can share our recommended retry/backoff policy: exponential backoff with jitter, max retries 3 for 5xx, client-side timeout slightly above your p99 target so you don't hang.
[02:40] Marta: That doc would be useful — our infra team is concerned about deduping and exactly-once semantics.
[02:45] Priya: We'll share a pattern: idempotency key + signature of messages (hash) so you can detect duplicates. Also the API supports a request_id header that surfaces in logs for debugging.
[02:58] Jared: How about generation params — we want control over randomness for assistant replies.
[03:02] Priya: Standard params: temperature, top_p, max_tokens, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty. For determinism we suggest temperature 0-0.2 and set seed-like controls where you need repeatable outputs. There's also sampling_mode in some models.
[03:20] Marta: And truncation — if input context is longer than model limit? We need to maintain the last 2 messages and trim older history.
[03:26] Priya: Redwood SDK has helper utilities for context window management — you can set tokenizer and approximate token counts; we also show recommendations per model (e.g., redwood-chat-large has 8k context). We'll send best-practice snippet.
[03:40] Samir: On the hosted side, model variants exist — smaller for cheaper/faster, larger for quality. We can route by policy if you want automatic fallback.
[03:49] Priyanka: Any limits we should know? Rate limiting?
[03:53] Samir: Hosted customers get quota defaults; by default there's a soft rate limit which you can raise. We expose per-route metrics and guide on batching. For spikes, Dedicated would be better but Hosted handles bursts with throttles and fallbacks.
[04:07] Marta: Can you explain per-token cost differences? We are cost-sensitive.
[04:11] Samir: Sure — smaller models are cheaper per token, and quantized variants further reduce cost. Redwood Optimize also gives recommendations per workload to minimize cost for a given quality target. We'll include a cost-examples spreadsheet.
[04:25] Jared: On retries again, for non-idempotent generation calls, how do you avoid double charges or double outputs?
[04:31] Priya: By using idempotency keys on the request; if a retry is received with same key we either return cached output or a record of prior call. For streaming where output was partial, it's trickier and we recommend client checkpointing and server-side resume where available.
[04:48] Marta: Security — SOC2, data retention, encryption, and SSO. We're a EU company and need data residency.
[04:55] Samir: Redwood is SOC2 and supports KMS integrations. Hosted can be configured with region selection for EU data residency; logs and metrics retention configurable. For strict compliance, we also offer Private deployment. We'll send security whitepaper and SOC2 report under NDA.
[05:10] Priya: Also note that for PII-sensitive prompts you can configure redaction and data retention policies.
[05:16] Jared: Any sample latency numbers for streaming? p95/p99?
[05:20] Priya: Typical streaming time-to-first-token is 80-200ms on our hosted infra for chat-medium model in NA region; p99 varies with payload size. We'll run a benchmark and share precise numbers for your prompt distribution.
[05:34] Priya (customer): If we do 10k messages/day, what's the onboarding?
[05:39] Samir: Onboarding is self-serve to start — quick signup, API keys, SDKs. For trial/pilot we can provision increased quotas and a short onboarding call to help with instrumentation. If you need SLAs and dedicated capacity that's a commercial step.
[05:54] Marta: For pilot, we'd like streaming samples and a small bench that mimics our 600-token contexts.
[05:59] Priya: We'll produce a benchmark harness you can run. It will generate typical length, measure p95/p99, token cost.
[06:08] Samir: Next steps recap — I’ll email pricing and the docs, Priya will share sample repo + retry patterns, Marta will provide prompt set by next week.
[06:16] Jared: One more quick question — what happens if model version is updated and we see regressions?
[06:21] Priya: We have rollout controls — you can pin versions, do canary rollouts, and Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring tied to your prompt/eval sets so you get alerts on regressions.
[06:34] Marta: Great. That helps.
[06:36] Priyanka: Ok thanks.
[06:38] Samir: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[06:42] Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-attribution and transcription artifacts; some proprietary product names slightly mangled (e.g., "redwood-chat-medium" may come through as "redwood chat medium" in the audio). References shared: https://redwood.ai/docs/hosted-api, streaming sample repo (link shared in follow-up email).
